CO:H25.summary: This vetoed proposal would have barred use of an automated driving system to drive a commercial motor vehicle unless a commercial driver's license holder is aboard, monitors the driving, and intervenes to avoid illegal or unsafe operation, sitting in the driver's seat if hazardous materials are carried. Fines would be $1,000 first offense, $2,000 second, doubling thereafter. Light-duty vehicles would be excluded.

Fines would be $1,000 first offense, $2,000 second, doubling thereafter. Light-duty vehicles would be excluded.
CO:H25.title: Automated Driving System Commercial Motor Vehicle

CO:H26.summary: This bill would prohibit driving a commercial motor vehicle with an automated driving system unless a person holding a commercial driver's license is aboard, monitoring and intervening if needed; that person would have to sit in the driver's seat when hazardous materials are carried. Penalties would start at $1,000, and the prohibition would be repealed September 1, 2031. The state patrol chief would report by November 1, 2030.
